findings.issue: Composition check on the {clock} ARGUMENT, not on the French value. checkpointAriaLabel() fills {clock} from checkpointClockLabel(), which at this head still builds a 12-hour `h:mm AM/PM` string by hand (checkpoint-model.ts:206-220, whose comment records 12-hour as a deliberate product decision - so this is a locale-conformance conflict, not an oversight). fr therefore renders « Aller à votre message du tour 3 sur 12, 3:45 PM » while the fr style guide requires 24-hour times. The French sentence itself is correct and no catalogue change can fix the shape.
findings.current: Aller à votre message du tour {turn, number} sur {total, number}, {clock}
findings.proposed: (no catalogue change) format {clock} with the fr 24-hour formatter - « 15:45 » - in checkpointClockLabel / formatMessageDateTime
findings.proposed_note: Code-level and pre-existing (inherited from formatMessageDateTime's `h:mm a`). Recorded again rather than dropped: it is unfixed at 80ee, and a `clean` row would hide it.

findings.issue: RESOLVED - prior NIT fr-wavea-2. The amendment adopts the proposed wording. Verified against the sidecar (accessible name of the composer landmark: the form holding the status row, the alert band, the interrupt notice and the box) and against the catalogue's own use of « zone de saisie » for the text FIELD (ui.agents.config.status.attached). « Zone de rédaction du message » names the composing region, is settled French UI vocabulary and reads natively. The sidecar's length hint ("Two words") describes the English; this string is an aria-label, never painted, so there is no width risk. Alternatives weighed and rejected: « Composeur de message » (an English calque no fr UI uses), « Zone de saisie du message » (the round-1 wording - names the field the catalogue already calls la zone de saisie), and « Zone de composition du message » (heavier, and « composition » in fr UI also means typesetting).

« Transcription » is the programme glossary's fr rendering for `transcript` and the corpus's own word for it (ui.chat.question_dock.secret_note, ui.chat.header.transcript_display, ui.settings.appearance.transcript_display_mode_setting.transcript_display, ui.chat.run_details.reader.no_transcript). It is accurate for the role=log region holding the messages and tool rows, and it removes the round-1 hazard that « Conversation » sat one letter from the sidebar's « Conversations ». Read back through the product's own accessors with the real fr catalogue registered: sidebar « Conversations », transcript « Transcription », composer « Zone de rédaction du message » - three distinct announced names. Alternatives weighed: « Fil de la conversation » (thread jargon, and not the glossary's word) and « Conversation en cours » (longer, and still one noun away from the sidebar's « Conversations »). The glossary row decides it: transcript -> transcription.

Stale ENGLISH documentation, not a defect in the French value: the sidecar says this key names "the transcript landmark and of the chat header landmark", but the header region root carries NO aria-label by design (chat-header.tsx:596-601, whose own comment says a landmark that is not `banner` is named by the section it heads and that §C4 named only three regions). chatRegionLabel("header") therefore has no shipped call site. Consequence for this audit: the value must be judged as the transcript's name, which « Transcription » is. Recorded so the next wave does not "fix" the header by wiring a transcript name onto it.
findings.proposed: (owner's call) narrow the sidecar's role/note to the transcript, or label the header deliberately with its own key
